2. `gh pr edit 2662` (`gh` 2.46.0) failed with `GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated ... (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)`, and `gh api ... --method PATCH` is denied by local permissions. A maintainer or a newer `gh` client must add the screenshot section below to the PR body before re-review.

Pinning and mutation check:
- `egui_app::tests::body_drag::shift_drag_snaps_to_the_bar_step_and_updates_the_value` and `egui_app::tests::body_turn::shift_drag_snaps_to_the_bar_angle_step` pin the Move and Rotate bar controls.
- Bypassing `viewport_bar::controls::draw` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` made both tests fail (RED). Restoring `shell.rs` made both pass (GREEN).

Gate and clippy:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 17/17 steps passed (`camcraft-ui` lib: 1227 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; 15 integration suites passed).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

Screenshot section ready for the PR body:

```markdown
## Viewport bar screenshots

These images show the viewport pane (`2x` scale) with the seeded `Block` selected. The headless GPU and egui shell render the 3D scene, handles, bottom bar, and control legend.

Before (`Move` off): the resting single-row bar sits at the bottom center.

![Viewport bar before with Move off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/505af4bae5d220b35074775984373140eac6d6b7/2662/before.png)

After (`Move` on): the bar expands upward with the `X`, `Y`, `Z` buttons, distance field, `Set` button, and `Snap 1.0 mm (Shift)` control. The control legend lifts above the expanded bar.

![Viewport bar after with Move on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/505af4bae5d220b35074775984373140eac6d6b7/2662/after-move.png)

After (`Rotate` on): the bar expands upward with the `X`, `Y`, `Z` buttons, angle field, `Set` button, and `Snap 90° (Shift)` control. The control legend lifts above the expanded bar.

![Viewport bar after with Rotate on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/505af4bae5d220b35074775984373140eac6d6b7/2662/after-rotate.png)

The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch at `505af4bae5d220b35074775984373140eac6d6b7`. No image or capture code is on the PR branch.
```

**Needs changes before merge: the merged quick gate is red.** The four failed tests also fail on unmodified upstream main.

### Earlier finding

The screenshot request is met. The body links the before, Move, and Rotate images from the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. I opened all three images. The PR adds no image file or capture code. The later author comment permits this review of the same head.

### What looks good

- Typed values use the existing undoable `MoveModelBy` and `TurnModelBy` paths. Tests check undo and stale toolpaths.
- The drag keeps the raw value separate from its snapped value. Shift can change during a drag.
- Input checks reject non-finite values. Zero values add no history step.
- The decision record explains the defaults and the choices. No new command or MCP tool is needed.
- I checked the current laws in `upstream/main:AGENTS.md`. The PR changes no process file, dependency, build script, fixture, or golden.

### Results: local trial merge

Base: `upstream/main` at `971c23faa026865be47e425a660439f8c3d17ecd`. The trial merge is clean. All UI suites ran from `crates/ui`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **16/17 steps passed**. The build passed. The UI library had 1260 passed, 4 failed, and 7 ignored tests.
- All 15 integration suites passed: boundary (3), boundary_picks (7), catalog_render (1), feedback (7), fixtures (7), gpu_render (11), machine (6), models (4), operations (31), shell (21), sinker_setup (2), tap_hand (3), theme_example (3), theme_files (17), waterjet_tool (1). Catalog_render and gpu_render each had one ignored test.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The first cached build stopped advancing. I interrupted it and ran the gate with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER=`. The completed results above use that run.

### Requested before merge

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/frame_cost_probe.rs:278`: restore a green merged quick gate. Four tests fail with the same assertion:

   ```text
   the area preview is filled
   ```

   Failed tests:
   - `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_caches::pick_chips_group_the_welded_faces_once_and_follow_the_picks`
   - `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_caches::pick_lines_build_once_per_input`
   - `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::area_preview_fill_is_made_once_per_draft`
   - `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`

   I also ran `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib egui_app::tests::frame_cost_ -- --test-threads=6` on unmodified main at the base SHA above. It had 1 passed and the same 4 failed tests at line 278. This is a base failure. Re-run the merged gate after the main fix is available. The required green gate is still missing, so `needs-rework` remains and the PR stays a draft.

### Mutations

I checked this as safety-tier work because these controls change model placement. I changed files only in the local review worktree and restored them after each check.

1. Bypass both snap branches in `move_drag::motion_snapped` and `resnap`: `body_drag::shift_drag_snaps_to_the_bar_step_and_updates_the_value` failed with `8.727707150785719` instead of an integer step. After restoration, it passed.
2. Bypass both snap branches in `turn_drag::motion_snapped` and `resnap`: `body_turn::shift_drag_snaps_to_the_bar_angle_step` failed with `51.56611154962022` instead of 90 degrees. After restoration, it passed.

No golden changed, so no golden comparison was required.

### Extra suites run

The main comparison above ran the five `frame_cost_` tests. The fixture and importer selection rules add no suites: the PR changes no fixture directory, STEP fixture, or importer. Kernel STEP and machining_mesh suites, and `feature_edge_g1_join`, were not required by this diff.

Release-lane pixel snapshots and an interactive desktop session were not run. This feature remains subject to the minor-cut merge rule.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
